name: Three.js Shading Language
role: Node-based shader authoring in JavaScript that compiles to WGSL or GLSL
summary: Node-graph shader language written as JavaScript functions, shipped inside Three.js as three/tsl. A NodeBuilder compiles it to WGSL for WebGPU or GLSL for WebGL2, so one material source targets both. Used through NodeMaterial classes with time and uniform nodes. Distinguishing strength: composable materials and post effects without string-built GLSL.
use_when: Over raw GLSL ShaderMaterial for materials that should run on WebGPU and WebGL2
Procedural materials with animated uniforms driven by a time node you control
Post effects built from nodes rather than the postprocessing package
avoid_when: Existing GLSL snippets or glslify modules: ShaderMaterial in Three.js
Shaders outside Three.js: regl, OGL or glslcanvas
notes: 2026-10-26: API churn between Three.js releases is expected, so pin the three version; the wiki page states no stability level.

assessment.rationale: Part of Three.js, released roughly monthly; the wiki spec was last edited 2026-06-24. The official_url wiki page is reachable; threejs.org/docs/TSL.html returned 404.
